heading: Application for notification
clause: A conformity assessment body shall submit an application for notification under this Directive to the notifying authority of the Member State in which it is established.

heading: Application for notification
clause: The application referred to in paragraph 1 shall be accompanied by a description of the conformity assessment activities, the conformity assessment module or modules and the toy or toys for which that body claims to be competent, as well as by an accreditation certificate, where one exists, issued by a national accreditation body attesting that the conformity assessment body fulfils the requirements laid down in Article 26.

heading: Application for notification
clause: Where the conformity assessment body concerned cannot provide an accreditation certificate, it shall provide the notifying authority with the documentary evidence necessary for the verification, recognition and regular monitoring of its compliance with the requirements laid down in Article 26.

heading: Notification procedure
clause: Notifying authorities may only notify conformity assessment bodies which have satisfied the requirements laid down in Article 26.

heading: Notification procedure
clause: Notifying authorities shall notify conformity assessment bodies to the Commission and the other Member States using the electronic notification tool developed and managed by the Commission.

heading: Notification procedure
clause: The notification shall include full details of the conformity assessment activities, the conformity assessment module or modules, toy or toys concerned and the relevant attestation of competence.

heading: Notification procedure
clause: Where a notification is not based on an accreditation certificate as referred to in Article 30(2), the notifying authority shall provide the Commission and the other Member States with documentary evidence which attests to the conformity assessment body’s competence and the arrangements in place to ensure that that body will be monitored regularly and will continue to satisfy the requirements laid down in Article 26.

heading: Notification procedure
marker: may perform the activities of a notified body only where
clause: The body concerned may perform the activities of a notified body only where no objections are raised by the Commission or the other Member States within two weeks of a notification where an accreditation certificate is used or within two months of a notification where accreditation is not used.

heading: Notification procedure
clause: The Commission and the other Member States shall be notified of any subsequent relevant changes to the notification.

heading: Identification numbers and lists of notified bodies
clause: The Commission shall assign an identification number to each notified body.

heading: Identification numbers and lists of notified bodies
clause: It shall assign a single identification number even where the same body is notified under several Community acts.

heading: Identification numbers and lists of notified bodies
clause: The Commission shall make publicly available a list of bodies notified under this Directive, including the identification numbers that have been allocated to them and the activities for which they have been notified.

heading: Identification numbers and lists of notified bodies
clause: The Commission shall ensure that the list is kept up to date.

heading: Changes to notifications
clause: Where a notifying authority has ascertained or has been informed that a notified body no longer meets the requirements laid down in Article 26, or that it is failing to fulfil its obligations, the notifying authority shall restrict, suspend or withdraw notification as appropriate, depending on the seriousness of the failure to meet those requirements or fulfil those obligations.

heading: Changes to notifications
clause: It shall immediately inform the Commission and the other Member States accordingly.

heading: Changes to notifications
clause: In the event of restriction, suspension or withdrawal of notification, or where the notified body has ceased its activity, the notifying Member State shall take appropriate steps to ensure that the files of that body are either processed by another notified body or kept available to the responsible notifying and market surveillance authorities, at their request.

heading: Challenge to the competence of notified bodies
clause: The Commission shall investigate all cases where it doubts, or doubt is brought to its attention regarding, the competence of a notified body or the continued fulfilment by a notified body of the requirements and responsibilities to which it is subject.

heading: Challenge to the competence of notified bodies
clause: The notifying Member State shall provide the Commission, on request, with all information relating to the basis for the notification or the maintenance of the competence of the body concerned.

heading: Challenge to the competence of notified bodies
clause: The Commission shall ensure that all sensitive information obtained in the course of its investigations is treated confidentially.

heading: Challenge to the competence of notified bodies
clause: Where the Commission ascertains that a notified body does not meet or no longer meets the requirements for notification, it shall inform the notifying Member State accordingly and request it to take the necessary corrective measures, including de-notification if necessary.

heading: Operational obligations of notified bodies
clause: Notified bodies shall carry out conformity assessments in accordance with the conformity assessment procedure provided for in Article 20.

heading: Operational obligations of notified bodies
clause: Conformity assessments shall be carried out in a proportionate manner, avoiding unnecessary burdens for economic operators.

heading: Operational obligations of notified bodies
clause: Conformity assessment bodies shall perform their activities taking due account of the size of an undertaking, the sector in which it operates, its structure, the degree of complexity of the technology of the toy in question and the mass or serial nature of the production process.

heading: Operational obligations of notified bodies
clause: In so doing, they shall nevertheless respect the degree of rigour and the level of protection required for the compliance of the toy with this Directive.

heading: Operational obligations of notified bodies
clause: Where a notified body finds that the requirements set out in Article 10 and Annex II or in corresponding harmonised standards have not been met by a manufacturer, it shall require that manufacturer to take appropriate corrective measures and shall not issue the EC-type examination certificate as referred to in Article 20(4).

heading: Operational obligations of notified bodies
clause: Where a notified body finds that the requirements set out in Article 10 and Annex II or in corresponding harmonised standards have not been met by a manufacturer, it shall require that manufacturer to take appropriate corrective measures and shall not issue the EC-type examination certificate as referred to in Article 20(4).

heading: Operational obligations of notified bodies
clause: Where, in the course of the monitoring of conformity following the issue of a EC-type examination certificate, a notified body finds that a toy is no longer in compliance, it shall require the manufacturer to take appropriate corrective measures, and shall suspend or withdraw the EC-type examination certificate if necessary.

heading: Operational obligations of notified bodies
clause: Where, in the course of the monitoring of conformity following the issue of a EC-type examination certificate, a notified body finds that a toy is no longer in compliance, it shall require the manufacturer to take appropriate corrective measures, and shall suspend or withdraw the EC-type examination certificate if necessary.

heading: Operational obligations of notified bodies
clause: Where corrective measures are not taken or do not have the required effect, the notified body shall restrict, suspend or withdraw any EC-type examination certificates, as appropriate.

heading: Information obligation of notified bodies
clause: Notified bodies shall inform the notifying authority of the following:

heading: Information obligation of notified bodies
clause: Notified bodies shall provide the other bodies notified under this Directive which carry out similar conformity assessment activities covering the same toys with relevant information on issues relating to negative and, on request, positive conformity assessment results.

heading: Exchange of experience
clause: The Commission shall provide for the organisation of exchange of experience between the Member States' national authorities responsible for notification policy.

heading: Coordination of notified bodies
clause: The Commission shall ensure that appropriate coordination and cooperation between bodies notified under this Directive are put in place and properly operated in the form of a sectoral group or groups of notified bodies.

heading: Coordination of notified bodies
clause: Member States shall ensure that the bodies notified by them participate in the work of that group or groups, directly or by means of designated representatives.

heading: Precautionary principle
clause: When competent authorities of the Member States take measures as provided for in this Directive, and in particular those referred to in Article 40, they shall take due account of the precautionary principle.

heading: General obligation to organise market surveillance
clause: Member States shall organise and perform surveillance of toys placed on the market in accordance with Articles 15 to 29 of Regulation (EC) No 765/2008.

heading: Instructions to the notified body
clause: If a market surveillance authority finds that a toy is not in conformity with the requirements set out in Article 10 and Annex II, it shall, where appropriate, instruct the notified body to withdraw the EC-type examination certificate in respect of that toy.

heading: Instructions to the notified body
clause: Where necessary, and in particular in the cases specified in the second subparagraph of Article 20(4), the market surveillance authority shall instruct the notified body to review the EC-type examination certificate.

heading: Procedure for dealing with toys presenting a risk at national level
clause: Where the market surveillance authorities of one Member State have taken action pursuant to Article 20 of Regulation (EC) No 765/2008, or where they have sufficient reason to believe that a toy covered by this Directive presents a risk to the health or safety of persons, they shall carry out an evaluation in relation to the toy concerned covering all the requirements laid down in this Directive.

heading: Procedure for dealing with toys presenting a risk at national level
clause: The relevant economic operators shall cooperate as necessary with the market surveillance authorities.

heading: Procedure for dealing with toys presenting a risk at national level
clause: Where, in the course of that evaluation, the market surveillance authorities find that the toy does not comply with the requirements laid down in this Directive, they shall without delay require the relevant economic operator to take appropriate corrective action to bring the toy into compliance with those requirements, to withdraw the toy from the market, or to recall it within a reasonable period, commensurate with the nature of the risk, as they may prescribe.

heading: Procedure for dealing with toys presenting a risk at national level
clause: The market surveillance authorities shall inform the relevant notified body accordingly.

heading: Procedure for dealing with toys presenting a risk at national level
clause: Where the market surveillance authorities consider that non-compliance is not restricted to their national territory, they shall inform the Commission and the other Member States of the results of the evaluation and of the actions which they have required the relevant economic operator to take.

heading: Procedure for dealing with toys presenting a risk at national level
clause: The relevant economic operator shall ensure that appropriate corrective action is taken in respect of toys which that operator has made available on the Community market.

heading: Procedure for dealing with toys presenting a risk at national level
clause: Where the relevant economic operator does not take adequate corrective action within the period referred to in the second subparagraph of paragraph 1, the market surveillance authorities shall take appropriate provisional measures to prohibit or restrict the toy being made available on their national market, to withdraw the toy from that market or to recall it.

heading: Procedure for dealing with toys presenting a risk at national level
clause: They shall inform the Commission and the other Member States, without delay, of those measures.

heading: Procedure for dealing with toys presenting a risk at national level
clause: The information referred to in paragraph 4 shall include all available details, in particular the data necessary for the identification of the non-compliant toy, the origin of the toy, the nature of the alleged non-compliance and the risk involved, the nature and duration of the national measures taken and the arguments put forward by the relevant economic operator.

heading: Procedure for dealing with toys presenting a risk at national level
clause: In particular, the market surveillance authorities shall indicate whether the non-compliance is due to either:

heading: Procedure for dealing with toys presenting a risk at national level
clause: Member States other than the Member State initiating the procedure shall without delay inform the Commission and the other Member States of any measures adopted and of any additional information at their disposal relating to the non-compliance of the toy concerned, and, in the event of disagreement with the notified national measure, of their objections.

heading: Procedure for dealing with toys presenting a risk at national level
clause: Member States shall ensure that appropriate restrictive measures are taken in respect of the toy concerned, such as withdrawal of the toy from their market, without delay.

heading: Community safeguard procedure
clause: Where, on completion of the procedure set out in Article 42(3) and (4), objections are raised against a measure taken by a Member State, or where the Commission considers a national measure to be contrary to Community legislation, the Commission shall without delay enter into consultation with the Member States and the relevant economic operator or operators and shall evaluate the national measure.

heading: Community safeguard procedure
clause: Where, on completion of the procedure set out in Article 42(3) and (4), objections are raised against a measure taken by a Member State, or where the Commission considers a national measure to be contrary to Community legislation, the Commission shall without delay enter into consultation with the Member States and the relevant economic operator or operators and shall evaluate the national measure.

heading: Community safeguard procedure
clause: On the basis of the results of that evaluation, the Commission shall decide whether the national measure is justified or not.

heading: Community safeguard procedure
clause: The Commission shall address its decision to all Member States and shall immediately communicate it to them and the relevant economic operator or operators.

heading: Community safeguard procedure
clause: The Commission shall address its decision to all Member States and shall immediately communicate it to them and the relevant economic operator or operators.

heading: Community safeguard procedure
clause: If the national measure is considered justified, all Member States shall take the measures necessary to ensure that the non-compliant toy is withdrawn from their market, and shall inform the Commission accordingly.

heading: Community safeguard procedure
clause: If the national measure is considered justified, all Member States shall take the measures necessary to ensure that the non-compliant toy is withdrawn from their market, and shall inform the Commission accordingly.

heading: Community safeguard procedure
clause: If the national measure is considered unjustified, the Member State concerned shall withdraw it.

heading: Community safeguard procedure
clause: Where the national measure is considered to be justified and the non-compliance of the toy is attributed to shortcomings in the harmonised standards referred to in Article 42(5)(b), the Commission shall inform the relevant European standardisation body or bodies and shall bring the matter before the Committee set up by Article 5 of Directive 98/34/EC.

heading: Community safeguard procedure
clause: Where the national measure is considered to be justified and the non-compliance of the toy is attributed to shortcomings in the harmonised standards referred to in Article 42(5)(b), the Commission shall inform the relevant European standardisation body or bodies and shall bring the matter before the Committee set up by Article 5 of Directive 98/34/EC.

heading: Community safeguard procedure
clause: That Committee shall consult the relevant European standardisation body or bodies and deliver its opinion without delay.

heading: Exchange of information — Community Rapid Information Exchange System
clause: If a measure referred to in Article 42(4) is a type of measure which is required under Article 22 of Regulation (EC) No 765/2008 to be notified through the Community Rapid Information Exchange System, it shall not be necessary to make a separate notification under Article 42(4) of this Directive, provided that the following conditions are met:

clause: Without prejudice to Article 42, where a Member State makes one of the following findings, it shall require the relevant economic operator to put an end to the non-compliance concerned:

heading: Formal non-compliance
clause: Where the non-compliance referred to in paragraph 1 persists, the Member State concerned shall take appropriate measures to restrict or prohibit the toy being made available on the market, or shall ensure that it is recalled or withdrawn from the market.

heading: Formal non-compliance
clause: Where the non-compliance referred to in paragraph 1 persists, the Member State concerned shall take appropriate measures to restrict or prohibit the toy being made available on the market, or shall ensure that it is recalled or withdrawn from the market.

heading: Amendments and implementing measures
clause: The Commission shall amend Appendix C to Annex II to this Directive accordingly.

heading: Amendments and implementing measures
clause: Those measures, designed to amend non-essential elements of this Directive by supplementing it, shall be adopted in accordance with the regulatory procedure with scrutiny referred to in Article 47(2) of this Directive.

heading: Amendments and implementing measures
clause: Those measures, designed to amend non-essential elements of this Directive by supplementing it, shall be adopted in accordance with the regulatory procedure with scrutiny referred to in Article 47(2).

heading: Committee procedure
clause: The Commission shall be assisted by a committee.

heading: Reporting
clause: By 20 July 2014 and every five years thereafter, Member States shall send the Commission a report on the application of this Directive.

heading: Reporting
clause: That report shall contain an evaluation of the situation concerning the safety of toys and of the effectiveness of this Directive, as well as a presentation of the market surveillance activities performed by that Member State.

heading: Reporting
clause: The Commission shall draw up and publish a summary of the national reports.

heading: Motivation of measures
clause: Any measure taken pursuant to this Directive to prohibit or restrict the placing on the market of a toy, to withdraw a toy or to recall a toy from the market shall state the exact grounds on which it is based.

heading: Motivation of measures

heading: PARTICULAR SAFETY REQUIREMENTS
clause: Toys and their parts and, in the case of fixed toys, their anchorages, must have the requisite mechanical strength and, where appropriate, stability to withstand the stresses to which they are subjected during use without breaking or becoming liable to distortion at the risk of causing physical injury.

heading: PARTICULAR SAFETY REQUIREMENTS
clause: Accessible edges, protrusions, cords, cables and fastenings on toys must be designed and manufactured in such a way that the risks of physical injury from contact with them are reduced as far as possible.

heading: PARTICULAR SAFETY REQUIREMENTS
clause: Toys must be designed and manufactured in such a way as not to present any risk or only the minimum risk inherent to their use which could be caused by the movement of their parts.

heading: PARTICULAR SAFETY REQUIREMENTS
clause: Toys and their parts must not present a risk of strangulation.

heading: PARTICULAR SAFETY REQUIREMENTS
clause: Toys and their parts must not present a risk of asphyxiation by closing off the flow of air as a result of airway obstruction external to the mouth and nose.

heading: PARTICULAR SAFETY REQUIREMENTS
clause: Toys and their parts must be of such dimensions as to not present a risk of asphyxiation by closing off the flow of air as a result of internal airway obstruction by objects wedged in the mouth or pharynx or lodged over the entrance to the lower airways.

heading: PARTICULAR SAFETY REQUIREMENTS
clause: Toys, which are clearly intended for use by children under 36 months, and their component parts and any of their detachable parts must be of such dimensions as to prevent their being swallowed or inhaled.

clause: The packaging in which toys are contained for retail sale must not present a risk of strangulation or asphyxiation caused by airway obstruction external to the mouth and nose.

clause: Toys contained within food or co-mingled with food must have their own packaging.

heading: Formal requirements for distance contracts

heading: Formal requirements for distance contracts

heading: Formal requirements for distance contracts

heading: Formal requirements for distance contracts

heading: Formal requirements for distance contracts
clause: Member States shall not impose any further formal pre-contractual information requirements for the fulfilment of the information obligations laid down in this Directive.

heading: Right of withdrawal
clause: Save where the exceptions provided for in Article 16 apply, the consumer shall have a period of 14 days to withdraw from a distance or off-premises contract, without giving any reason, and without incurring any costs other than those provided for in Article 13(2) and Article 14.

heading: Right of withdrawal
clause: The Member States shall not prohibit the contracting parties from performing their contractual obligations during the withdrawal period.

heading: Exercise of the right of withdrawal
clause: Before the expiry of the withdrawal period, the consumer shall inform the trader of his decision to withdraw from the contract.

heading: Exercise of the right of withdrawal

heading: Exercise of the right of withdrawal
clause: The consumer shall have exercised his right of withdrawal within the withdrawal period referred to in Article 9(2) and Article 10 if the communication concerning the exercise of the right of withdrawal is sent by the consumer before that period has expired.

heading: Exercise of the right of withdrawal
clause: In those cases the trader shall communicate to the consumer an acknowledgement of receipt of such a withdrawal on a durable medium without delay.

heading: Exercise of the right of withdrawal
clause: The burden of proof of exercising the right of withdrawal in accordance with this Article shall be on the consumer.

heading: Obligations of the trader in the event of withdrawal
clause: The trader shall reimburse all payments received from the consumer, including, if applicable, the costs of delivery without undue delay and in any event not later than 14 days from the day on which he is informed of the consumer’s decision to withdraw from the contract in accordance with Article 11.

heading: Obligations of the trader in the event of withdrawal
clause: The trader shall carry out the reimbursement referred to in the first subparagraph using the same means of payment as the consumer used for the initial transaction, unless the consumer has expressly agreed otherwise and provided that the consumer does not incur any fees as a result of such reimbursement.

heading: Obligations of the trader in the event of withdrawal
clause: Notwithstanding paragraph 1, the trader shall not be required to reimburse the supplementary costs, if the consumer has expressly opted for a type of delivery other than the least expensive type of standard delivery offered by the trader.

heading: Obligations of the consumer in the event of withdrawal
clause: Unless the trader has offered to collect the goods himself, the consumer shall send back the goods or hand them over to the trader or to a person authorised by the trader to receive the goods, without undue delay and in any event not later than 14 days from the day on which he has communicated his decision to withdraw from the contract to the trader in accordance with Article 11.

heading: Obligations of the consumer in the event of withdrawal

heading: Obligations of the consumer in the event of withdrawal

heading: Obligations of the consumer in the event of withdrawal
clause: The consumer shall only bear the direct cost of returning the goods unless the trader has agreed to bear them or the trader failed to inform the consumer that the consumer has to bear them.

heading: Obligations of the consumer in the event of withdrawal
clause: In the case of off-premises contracts where the goods have been delivered to the consumer’s home at the time of the conclusion of the contract, the trader shall at his own expense collect the goods if, by their nature, those goods cannot normally be returned by post.

heading: Obligations of the consumer in the event of withdrawal
clause: The consumer shall in any event not be liable for diminished value of the goods where the trader has failed to provide notice of the right of withdrawal in accordance with point (h) of Article 6(1).

heading: Obligations of the consumer in the event of withdrawal
clause: Where a consumer exercises the right of withdrawal after having made a request in accordance with Article 7(3) or Article 8(8), the consumer shall pay to the trader an amount which is in proportion to what has been provided until the time the consumer has informed the trader of the exercise of the right of withdrawal, in comparison with the full coverage of the contract.

clause: Except as provided for in Article 13(2) and in this Article, the consumer shall not incur any liability as a consequence of the exercise of the right of withdrawal.

heading: Effects of the exercise of the right of withdrawal on ancillary contracts
clause: The Member States shall lay down detailed rules on the termination of such contracts.

heading: Exceptions from the right of withdrawal
clause: Member States shall not provide for the right of withdrawal set out in Articles 9 to 15 in respect of distance and off-premises contracts as regards the following:

heading: Delivery
clause: Unless the parties have agreed otherwise on the time of delivery, the trader shall deliver the goods by transferring the physical possession or control of the goods to the consumer without undue delay, but not later than 30 days from the conclusion of the contract.

heading: Delivery
clause: Where the trader has failed to fulfil his obligation to deliver the goods at the time agreed upon with the consumer or within the time limit set out in paragraph 1, the consumer shall call upon him to make the delivery within an additional period of time appropriate to the circumstances.

heading: Delivery
clause: The first subparagraph shall not be applicable to sales contracts where the trader has refused to deliver the goods or where delivery within the agreed delivery period is essential taking into account all the circumstances attending the conclusion of the contract or where the consumer informs the trader, prior to the conclusion of the contract, that delivery by or on a specified date is essential.

heading: Delivery
clause: Upon termination of the contract, the trader shall, without undue delay, reimburse all sums paid under the contract.

heading: Fees for the use of means of payment
clause: Member States shall prohibit traders from charging consumers, in respect of the use of a given means of payment, fees that exceed the cost borne by the trader for the use of such means.

heading: Passing of risk
clause: In contracts where the trader dispatches the goods to the consumer, the risk of loss of or damage to the goods shall pass to the consumer when he or a third party indicated by the consumer and other than the carrier has acquired the physical possession of the goods.

heading: Passing of risk
clause: However, the risk shall pass to the consumer upon delivery to the carrier if the carrier was commissioned by the consumer to carry the goods and that choice was not offered by the trader, without prejudice to the rights of the consumer against the carrier.

heading: Communication by telephone
clause: Member States shall ensure that where the trader operates a telephone line for the purpose of contacting him by telephone in relation to the contract concluded, the consumer, when contacting the trader is not bound to pay more than the basic rate.

heading: Additional payments
clause: Before the consumer is bound by the contract or offer, the trader shall seek the express consent of the consumer to any extra payment in addition to the remuneration agreed upon for the trader’s main contractual obligation.

heading: Additional payments
clause: If the trader has not obtained the consumer’s express consent but has inferred it by using default options which the consumer is required to reject in order to avoid the additional payment, the consumer shall be entitled to reimbursement of this payment.

heading: Enforcement
clause: Member States shall ensure that adequate and effective means exist to ensure compliance with this Directive.

heading: Enforcement
clause: The means referred to in paragraph 1 shall include provisions whereby one or more of the following bodies, as determined by national law, may take action under national law before the courts or before the competent administrative bodies to ensure that the national provisions transposing this Directive are applied:

heading: Penalties
clause: Member States shall lay down the rules on penalties applicable to infringements of the national provisions adopted pursuant to this Directive and shall take all measures necessary to ensure that they are implemented.

heading: Penalties
clause: Member States shall lay down the rules on penalties applicable to infringements of the national provisions adopted pursuant to this Directive and shall take all measures necessary to ensure that they are implemented.

heading: Penalties
clause: The penalties provided for must be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.

heading: Penalties

heading: Penalties

heading: Imperative nature of the Directive
clause: If the law applicable to the contract is the law of a Member State, consumers may not waive the rights conferred on them by the national measures transposing this Directive.

heading: Information
clause: Member States shall take appropriate measures to inform consumers and traders of the national provisions transposing this Directive and shall, where appropriate, encourage traders and code owners as defined in point (g) of Article 2 of Directive 2005/29/EC, to inform consumers of their codes of conduct.

heading: Information
clause: Member States shall take appropriate measures to inform consumers and traders of the national provisions transposing this Directive and shall, where appropriate, encourage traders and code owners as defined in point (g) of Article 2 of Directive 2005/29/EC, to inform consumers of their codes of conduct.

heading: Inertia selling
clause: The consumer shall be exempted from the obligation to provide any consideration in cases of unsolicited supply of goods, water, gas, electricity, district heating or digital content or unsolicited provision of services, prohibited by Article 5(5) and point 29 of Annex I to Directive 2005/29/EC.

heading: Inertia selling
clause: In such cases, the absence of a response from the consumer following such an unsolicited supply or provision shall not constitute consent.

heading: Transposition
clause: Member States shall adopt and publish, by 13 December 2013, the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive.

heading: Transposition
clause: They shall forthwith communicate to the Commission the text of these measures in the form of documents.

heading: Transposition
clause: The Commission shall make use of these documents for the purposes of the report referred to in Article 30.

heading: Transposition
clause: When Member States adopt those measures, they shall contain a reference to this Directive or be accompanied by such a reference on the occasion of their official publication.

heading: Transposition
clause: Member States shall determine how such reference is to be made.

heading: Reporting requirements
clause: Where a Member State makes use of any of the regulatory choices referred to in Article 3(4), Article 6(7), Article 6(8), Article 7(4), Article 8(6) and Article 9(3), it shall inform the Commission thereof by 13 December 2013, as well as of any subsequent changes.

heading: Reporting requirements
clause: The Commission shall ensure that the information referred to in paragraph 1 is easily accessible to consumers and traders, inter alia, on a dedicated website.

heading: Reporting requirements
clause: The Commission shall forward the information referred to in paragraph 1 to the other Member States and the European Parliament.

heading: Reporting requirements
clause: The Commission shall consult stakeholders on that information.

heading: Reporting by the Commission and review
clause: By 13 December 2016, the Commission shall submit a report on the application of this Directive to the European Parliament and the Council.

heading: Reporting by the Commission and review
clause: That report shall include in particular an evaluation of the provisions of this Directive regarding digital content including the right of withdrawal.

heading: Reporting by the Commission and review
clause: The report shall be accompanied, where necessary, by legislative proposals to adapt this Directive to developments in the field of consumer rights.

heading: Subject matter
clause: This Directive lays down the rules and procedures under which the Member States shall cooperate with each other with a view to exchanging information that is foreseeably relevant to the administration and enforcement of the domestic laws of the Member States concerning the taxes referred to in Article 2.

heading: Organisation
clause: Each Member State shall inform the Commission, within one month from 11 March 2011, of its competent authority for the purposes of this Directive and shall inform the Commission without delay of any change thereto.

heading: Organisation
clause: Each Member State shall inform the Commission, within one month from 11 March 2011, of its competent authority for the purposes of this Directive and shall inform the Commission without delay of any change thereto.

heading: Organisation
clause: The Commission shall make the information available to the other Member States and publish a list of the authorities of the Member States in the Official Journal of the European Union .

heading: Organisation
clause: The competent authority shall designate a single central liaison office.

heading: Organisation
clause: The competent authority shall be responsible for informing the Commission and the other Member States thereof.

heading: Organisation
clause: The competent authority shall be responsible for informing the Commission thereof.

heading: Organisation
clause: The central liaison office shall be responsible for keeping the list of liaison departments up to date and making it available to the central liaison offices of the other Member States concerned and to the Commission.

heading: Organisation
clause: The central liaison office shall be responsible for keeping the list of competent officials up to date and making it available to the central liaison offices of the other Member States concerned and to the Commission.

heading: Organisation
clause: The officials engaged in administrative cooperation pursuant to this Directive shall in any case be deemed to be competent officials for that purpose, in accordance with arrangements laid down by the competent authorities.

heading: Organisation
clause: Where a liaison department or a competent official sends or receives a request or a reply to a request for cooperation, it shall inform the central liaison office of its Member State under the procedures laid down by that Member State.

heading: Organisation
clause: Where a liaison department or a competent official receives a request for cooperation requiring action which falls outside the competence it is assigned according to the national legislation or policy of its Member State, it shall forward such request without delay to the central liaison office of its Member State and inform the requesting authority thereof.

heading: Organisation
clause: In such a case, the period laid down in Article 7 shall start the day after the request for cooperation is forwarded to the central liaison office.

heading: Procedure for the exchange of information on request
clause: At the request of the requesting authority, the requested authority shall communicate to the requesting authority any information referred to in Article 1(1) that it has in its possession or that it obtains as a result of administrative enquiries.

heading: Administrative enquiries
clause: The requested authority shall arrange for the carrying out of any administrative enquiries necessary to obtain the information referred to in Article 5.

heading: Administrative enquiries
clause: If the requested authority takes the view that no administrative enquiry is necessary, it shall immediately inform the requesting authority of the reasons thereof.

heading: Administrative enquiries
clause: In order to obtain the requested information or to conduct the administrative enquiry requested, the requested authority shall follow the same procedures as it would when acting on its own initiative or at the request of another authority in its own Member State.

heading: Administrative enquiries
clause: When specifically requested by the requesting authority, the requested authority shall communicate original documents provided that this is not contrary to the provisions in force in the Member State of the requested authority.

heading: Time limits
clause: The requested authority shall provide the information referred to in Article 5 as quickly as possible, and no later than six months from the date of receipt of the request.

heading: Time limits
clause: However, where the requested authority is already in possession of that information, the information shall be transmitted within two months of that date.

heading: Time limits
clause: The requested authority shall confirm immediately and in any event no later than seven working days from receipt, if possible by electronic means, receipt of a request to the requesting authority.

heading: Time limits
clause: Within one month of receipt of the request, the requested authority shall notify the requesting authority of any deficiencies in the request and of the need for any additional background information.

heading: Time limits
clause: In such a case, the time limits provided for in paragraph 1 shall start the day after the requested authority has received the additional information needed.

heading: Time limits
clause: Where the requested authority is unable to respond to the request by the relevant time limit, it shall inform the requesting authority immediately and in any event within three months of the receipt of the request, of the reasons for its failure to do so, and the date by which it considers it might be able to respond.

heading: Time limits
clause: Where the requested authority is not in possession of the requested information and is unable to respond to the request for information or refuses to do so on the grounds provided for in Article 17, it shall inform the requesting authority of the reasons thereof immediately and in any event within one month of receipt of the request.

clause: The competent authority of each Member State shall, by automatic exchange, communicate to the competent authority of any other Member State, information regarding taxable periods as from 1 January 2014 that is available concerning residents in that other Member State, on the following specific categories of income and capital as they are to be understood under the national legislation of the Member State which communicates the information:

heading: Scope and conditions of mandatory automatic exchange of information
clause: Before 1 January 2014, Member States shall inform the Commission of the categories listed in paragraph 1 in respect of which they have information available.

heading: Scope and conditions of mandatory automatic exchange of information
clause: They shall inform the Commission of any subsequent changes thereto.

heading: Scope and conditions of mandatory automatic exchange of information
clause: It shall also inform the Commission thereof.

heading: Scope and conditions of mandatory automatic exchange of information
clause: Before 1 July 2016, Member States shall provide the Commission on an annual basis with statistics on the volume of automatic exchanges and, to the extent possible, with information on the administrative and other relevant costs and benefits relating to exchanges that have taken place and any potential changes, for both tax administrations and third parties.

heading: Scope and conditions of mandatory automatic exchange of information
clause: Before 1 July 2017, the Commission shall submit a report that provides an overview and an assessment of the statistics and information received, on issues such as the administrative and other relevant costs and benefits of the automatic exchange of information, as well as practical aspects linked thereto.

heading: Scope and conditions of mandatory automatic exchange of information
clause: If appropriate, the Commission shall present a proposal to the Council regarding the categories of income and capital and/or the conditions laid down in paragraph 1, including the condition that information concerning residents in other Member States has to be available.

heading: Scope and conditions of mandatory automatic exchange of information
clause: If appropriate, the Commission shall present a proposal to the Council regarding the categories of income and capital and/or the conditions laid down in paragraph 1, including the condition that information concerning residents in other Member States has to be available.

heading: Scope and conditions of mandatory automatic exchange of information
clause: When examining a proposal put forward by the Commission, the Council shall assess further strengthening of the efficiency and functioning of the automatic exchange of information and raising the standard thereof, with the aim of providing that:

heading: Scope and conditions of mandatory automatic exchange of information

clause: the competent authority of each Member State shall, by automatic exchange, communicate to the competent authority of any other Member State, information regarding taxable periods as from 1 January 2017 concerning residents in that other Member State, on at least three of the specific categories of income and capital listed in paragraph 1, as they are to be understood under the national legislation of the Member State communicating the information;

heading: Scope and conditions of mandatory automatic exchange of information
clause: The communication of information shall take place at least once a year, within six months following the end of the tax year of the Member State during which the information became available.

heading: Scope and conditions of mandatory automatic exchange of information
clause: The Commission shall adopt the practical arrangements for the automatic exchange of information, in accordance with the procedure referred to in Article 26(2), before the dates referred to in Article 29(1).

heading: Scope and conditions of mandatory automatic exchange of information
clause: Where Member States agree on the automatic exchange of information for additional categories of income and capital in bilateral or multilateral agreements which they conclude with other Member States, they shall communicate those agreements to the Commission which shall make those agreements available to all the other Member States

heading: Scope and conditions of mandatory automatic exchange of information
clause: Where Member States agree on the automatic exchange of information for additional categories of income and capital in bilateral or multilateral agreements which they conclude with other Member States, they shall communicate those agreements to the Commission which shall make those agreements available to all the other Member States

heading: Scope and conditions of spontaneous exchange of information
clause: The competent authority of each Member State shall communicate the information referred to in Article 1(1) to the competent authority of any other Member State concerned, in any of the following circumstances:

heading: Time limits
clause: The competent authority to which information referred to in Article 9(1) becomes available, shall forward that information to the competent authority of any other Member State concerned as quickly as possible, and no later than one month after it becomes available.

heading: Time limits
clause: The competent authority to which information is communicated pursuant to Article 9 shall confirm, if possible by electronic means, the receipt of the information to the competent authority which provided the information immediately and in any event no later than seven working days.

heading: Scope and conditions
chapeau: 1. By agreement between the requesting authority and the requested authority and in accordance with the arrangements laid down by the latter, officials authorised by the requesting authority may, with a view to exchanging the information referred to in Article 1(1):
clause: Where the requested information is contained in documentation to which the officials of the requested authority have access, the officials of the requesting authority shall be given copies thereof.

heading: Scope and conditions
clause: Any refusal by the person under investigation to respect the inspection measures of the officials of the requesting authority shall be treated by the requested authority as if that refusal was committed against officials of the latter authority.

heading: Scope and conditions
clause: Officials authorised by the requesting Member State present in another Member State in accordance with paragraph 1 shall at all times be able to produce written authority stating their identity and their official capacity.

heading: Simultaneous controls
clause: The competent authority in each Member State shall identify independently the persons for whom it intends to propose a simultaneous control.

heading: Simultaneous controls
clause: It shall notify the competent authority of the other Member States concerned of any cases for which it proposes a simultaneous control, giving reasons for its choice.

heading: Simultaneous controls
clause: It shall specify the period of time during which those controls are to be conducted.

heading: Simultaneous controls
clause: The competent authority of each Member State concerned shall decide whether it wishes to take part in simultaneous controls.

heading: Simultaneous controls
clause: It shall confirm its agreement or communicate its reasoned refusal to the authority that proposed a simultaneous control.

heading: Simultaneous controls
clause: The competent authority of each Member State concerned shall appoint a representative with responsibility for supervising and coordinating the control operation.

heading: Request for notification
clause: At the request of the competent authority of a Member State, the competent authority of another Member State shall, in accordance with the rules governing the notification of similar instruments in the requested Member State, notify the addressee of any instruments and decisions which emanate from the administrative authorities of the requesting Member State and concern the application in its territory of legislation on taxes covered by this Directive.

heading: Request for notification
clause: Requests for notification shall indicate the subject of the instrument or decision to be notified and shall specify the name and address of the addressee, together with any other information which may facilitate identification of the addressee.

heading: Request for notification
clause: Requests for notification shall indicate the subject of the instrument or decision to be notified and shall specify the name and address of the addressee, together with any other information which may facilitate identification of the addressee.

heading: Request for notification
clause: The requested authority shall inform the requesting authority immediately of its response and, in particular, of the date of notification of the instrument or decision to the addressee.

heading: Request for notification
clause: The requesting authority shall only make a request for notification pursuant to this Article when it is unable to notify in accordance with the rules governing the notification of the instruments concerned in the requesting Member State, or where such notification would give rise to disproportionate difficulties.

heading: Conditions
clause: If feedback is requested, the competent authority which received the information shall, without prejudice to the rules on tax secrecy and data protection applicable in its Member State, send feedback to the competent authority which provided the information as soon as possible and no later than three months after the outcome of the use of the requested information is known.

clause: The controller and processor shall take steps to ensure that any natural person acting under the authority of the controller or the processor who has access to personal data does not process them except on instructions from the controller, unless he or she is required to do so by Union or Member State law.

clause: The data protection officer shall be designated on the basis of professional qualities and, in particular, expert knowledge of data protection law and practices and the ability to fulfil the tasks referred to in Article 39.

clause: Each supervisory authority shall be competent for the performance of the tasks assigned to and the exercise of the powers conferred on it in accordance with this Regulation on the territory of its own Member State.

heading: Competence
clause: Where processing is carried out by public authorities or private bodies acting on the basis of point (c) or (e) of Article 6(1), the supervisory authority of the Member State concerned shall be competent.

heading: Competence
clause: Supervisory authorities shall not be competent to supervise processing operations of courts acting in their judicial capacity.

heading: Competence of the lead supervisory authority
clause: Without prejudice to Article 55, the supervisory authority of the main establishment or of the single establishment of the controller or processor shall be competent to act as lead supervisory authority for the cross-border processing carried out by that controller or processor in accordance with the procedure provided in Article 60.

heading: Competence of the lead supervisory authority
clause: By derogation from paragraph 1, each supervisory authority shall be competent to handle a complaint lodged with it or a possible infringement of this Regulation, if the subject matter relates only to an establishment in its Member State or substantially affects data subjects only in its Member State.

heading: Competence of the lead supervisory authority
clause: In the cases referred to in paragraph 2 of this Article, the supervisory authority shall inform the lead supervisory authority without delay on that matter.

heading: Competence of the lead supervisory authority
clause: Within a period of three weeks after being informed the lead supervisory authority shall decide whether or not it will handle the case in accordance with the procedure provided in Article 60, taking into account whether or not there is an establishment of the controller or processor in the Member State of which the supervisory authority informed it.

heading: Competence of the lead supervisory authority
clause: The lead supervisory authority shall take utmost account of that draft when preparing the draft decision referred to in Article 60(3).

heading: Competence of the lead supervisory authority
clause: Where the lead supervisory authority decides not to handle the case, the supervisory authority which informed the lead supervisory authority shall handle it according to Articles 61 and 62.

heading: Competence of the lead supervisory authority
clause: The lead supervisory authority shall be the sole interlocutor of the controller or processor for the cross-border processing carried out by that controller or processor.

heading: Powers

clause: Each Member State may provide by law that its supervisory authority shall have additional powers to those referred to in paragraphs 1, 2 and 3.

heading: Powers
clause: The exercise of those powers shall not impair the effective operation of Chapter VII.

clause: The lead supervisory authority shall cooperate with the other supervisory authorities concerned in accordance with this Article in an endeavour to reach consensus.

heading: Cooperation between the lead supervisory authority and the other supervisory authorities concerned
clause: The lead supervisory authority and the supervisory authorities concerned shall exchange all relevant information with each other.

heading: Cooperation between the lead supervisory authority and the other supervisory authorities concerned
clause: The lead supervisory authority shall, without delay, communicate the relevant information on the matter to the other supervisory authorities concerned.

heading: Cooperation between the lead supervisory authority and the other supervisory authorities concerned
clause: It shall without delay submit a draft decision to the other supervisory authorities concerned for their opinion and take due account of their views.

heading: Cooperation between the lead supervisory authority and the other supervisory authorities concerned
clause: Where any of the other supervisory authorities concerned within a period of four weeks after having been consulted in accordance with paragraph 3 of this Article, expresses a relevant and reasoned objection to the draft decision, the lead supervisory authority shall, if it does not follow the relevant and reasoned objection or is of the opinion that the objection is not relevant or reasoned, submit the matter to the consistency mechanism referred to in Article 63.

heading: Cooperation between the lead supervisory authority and the other supervisory authorities concerned
clause: Where the lead supervisory authority intends to follow the relevant and reasoned objection made, it shall submit to the other supervisory authorities concerned a revised draft decision for their opinion.

heading: Cooperation between the lead supervisory authority and the other supervisory authorities concerned
clause: That revised draft decision shall be subject to the procedure referred to in paragraph 4 within a period of two weeks.

heading: Cooperation between the lead supervisory authority and the other supervisory authorities concerned
clause: Where none of the other supervisory authorities concerned has objected to the draft decision submitted by the lead supervisory authority within the period referred to in paragraphs 4 and 5, the lead supervisory authority and the supervisory authorities concerned shall be deemed to be in agreement with that draft decision and shall be bound by it.

heading: Cooperation between the lead supervisory authority and the other supervisory authorities concerned
clause: The lead supervisory authority shall adopt and notify the decision to the main establishment or single establishment of the controller or processor, as the case may be and inform the other supervisory authorities concerned and the Board of the decision in question, including a summary of the relevant facts and grounds.

heading: Cooperation between the lead supervisory authority and the other supervisory authorities concerned
clause: The supervisory authority with which a complaint has been lodged shall inform the complainant on the decision.

heading: Cooperation between the lead supervisory authority and the other supervisory authorities concerned
clause: By derogation from paragraph 7, where a complaint is dismissed or rejected, the supervisory authority with which the complaint was lodged shall adopt the decision and notify it to the complainant and shall inform the controller thereof.

heading: Cooperation between the lead supervisory authority and the other supervisory authorities concerned
clause: By derogation from paragraph 7, where a complaint is dismissed or rejected, the supervisory authority with which the complaint was lodged shall adopt the decision and notify it to the complainant and shall inform the controller thereof.

heading: Cooperation between the lead supervisory authority and the other supervisory authorities concerned
clause: Where the lead supervisory authority and the supervisory authorities concerned agree to dismiss or reject parts of a complaint and to act on other parts of that complaint, a separate decision shall be adopted for each of those parts of the matter.

clause: The lead supervisory authority shall adopt the decision for the part concerning actions in relation to the controller, shall notify it to the main establishment or single establishment of the controller or processor on the territory of its Member State and shall inform the complainant thereof, while the supervisory authority of the complainant shall adopt the decision for the part concerning dismissal or rejection of that complaint, and shall notify it to that complainant and shall inform the controller or processor thereof.

clause: The lead supervisory authority shall adopt the decision for the part concerning actions in relation to the controller, shall notify it to the main establishment or single establishment of the controller or processor on the territory of its Member State and shall inform the complainant thereof, while the supervisory authority of the complainant shall adopt the decision for the part concerning dismissal or rejection of that complaint, and shall notify it to that complainant and shall inform the controller or processor thereof.

clause: The lead supervisory authority shall adopt the decision for the part concerning actions in relation to the controller, shall notify it to the main establishment or single establishment of the controller or processor on the territory of its Member State and shall inform the complainant thereof, while the supervisory authority of the complainant shall adopt the decision for the part concerning dismissal or rejection of that complaint, and shall notify it to that complainant and shall inform the controller or processor thereof.

heading: Cooperation between the lead supervisory authority and the other supervisory authorities concerned
clause: The lead supervisory authority shall adopt the decision for the part concerning actions in relation to the controller, shall notify it to the main establishment or single establishment of the controller or processor on the territory of its Member State and shall inform the complainant thereof, while the supervisory authority of the complainant shall adopt the decision for the part concerning dismissal or rejection of that complaint, and shall notify it to that complainant and shall inform the controller or processor thereof.

clause: The lead supervisory authority shall adopt the decision for the part concerning actions in relation to the controller, shall notify it to the main establishment or single establishment of the controller or processor on the territory of its Member State and shall inform the complainant thereof, while the supervisory authority of the complainant shall adopt the decision for the part concerning dismissal or rejection of that complaint, and shall notify it to that complainant and shall inform the controller or processor thereof.

heading: Cooperation between the lead supervisory authority and the other supervisory authorities concerned
clause: The lead supervisory authority shall adopt the decision for the part concerning actions in relation to the controller, shall notify it to the main establishment or single establishment of the controller or processor on the territory of its Member State and shall inform the complainant thereof, while the supervisory authority of the complainant shall adopt the decision for the part concerning dismissal or rejection of that complaint, and shall notify it to that complainant and shall inform the controller or processor thereof.

heading: Cooperation between the lead supervisory authority and the other supervisory authorities concerned
clause: After being notified of the decision of the lead supervisory authority pursuant to paragraphs 7 and 9, the controller or processor shall take the necessary measures to ensure compliance with the decision as regards processing activities in the context of all its establishments in the Union.

heading: Cooperation between the lead supervisory authority and the other supervisory authorities concerned
clause: The controller or processor shall notify the measures taken for complying with the decision to the lead supervisory authority, which shall inform the other supervisory authorities concerned.

clause: The controller or processor shall notify the measures taken for complying with the decision to the lead supervisory authority, which shall inform the other supervisory authorities concerned.

heading: Cooperation between the lead supervisory authority and the other supervisory authorities concerned
clause: The lead supervisory authority and the other supervisory authorities concerned shall supply the information required under this Article to each other by electronic means, using a standardised format.

heading: Mutual assistance
clause: Supervisory authorities shall provide each other with relevant information and mutual assistance in order to implement and apply this Regulation in a consistent manner, and shall put in place measures for effective cooperation with one another.

heading: Mutual assistance
clause: Supervisory authorities shall provide each other with relevant information and mutual assistance in order to implement and apply this Regulation in a consistent manner, and shall put in place measures for effective cooperation with one another.

heading: Mutual assistance
clause: Mutual assistance shall cover, in particular, information requests and supervisory measures, such as requests to carry out prior authorisations and consultations, inspections and investigations.

heading: Mutual assistance
clause: Each supervisory authority shall take all appropriate measures required to reply to a request of another supervisory authority without undue delay and no later than one month after receiving the request.

heading: Mutual assistance
clause: Requests for assistance shall contain all the necessary information, including the purpose of and reasons for the request.

heading: Mutual assistance
clause: Information exchanged shall be used only for the purpose for which it was requested.

heading: Mutual assistance
clause: The requested supervisory authority shall not refuse to comply with the request unless:

heading: Mutual assistance
clause: The requested supervisory authority shall inform the requesting supervisory authority of the results or, as the case may be, of the progress of the measures taken in order to respond to the request.

heading: Mutual assistance
clause: The requested supervisory authority shall provide reasons for any refusal to comply with a request pursuant to paragraph 4.

heading: Mutual assistance
clause: Requested supervisory authorities shall, as a rule, supply the information requested by other supervisory authorities by electronic means, using a standardised format.

heading: Mutual assistance
clause: Requested supervisory authorities shall not charge a fee for any action taken by them pursuant to a request for mutual assistance.

heading: Mutual assistance
clause: Those implementing acts shall be adopted in accordance with the examination procedure referred to in Article 93(2).

heading: Joint operations of supervisory authorities
clause: The supervisory authorities shall, where appropriate, conduct joint operations including joint investigations and joint enforcement measures in which members or staff of the supervisory authorities of other Member States are involved.

heading: Joint operations of supervisory authorities
clause: The supervisory authority which is competent pursuant to Article 56(1) or (4) shall invite the supervisory authority of each of those Member States to take part in the joint operations and shall respond without delay to the request of a supervisory authority to participate.

heading: Joint operations of supervisory authorities
clause: The supervisory authority which is competent pursuant to Article 56(1) or (4) shall invite the supervisory authority of each of those Member States to take part in the joint operations and shall respond without delay to the request of a supervisory authority to participate.

heading: Joint operations of supervisory authorities
clause: The seconding supervisory authority's members or staff shall be subject to the Member State law of the host supervisory authority.

heading: Joint operations of supervisory authorities
clause: Where, in accordance with paragraph 1, staff of a seconding supervisory authority operate in another Member State, the Member State of the host supervisory authority shall assume responsibility for their actions, including liability, for any damage caused by them during their operations, in accordance with the law of the Member State in whose territory they are operating.

heading: Joint operations of supervisory authorities
clause: The Member State in whose territory the damage was caused shall make good such damage under the conditions applicable to damage caused by its own staff.

heading: Joint operations of supervisory authorities
clause: The Member State of the seconding supervisory authority whose staff has caused damage to any person in the territory of another Member State shall reimburse that other Member State in full any sums it has paid to the persons entitled on their behalf.

heading: Joint operations of supervisory authorities
clause: Without prejudice to the exercise of its rights vis-à-vis third parties and with the exception of paragraph 5, each Member State shall refrain, in the case provided for in paragraph 1, from requesting reimbursement from another Member State in relation to damage referred to in paragraph 4.

heading: Consistency mechanism
clause: In order to contribute to the consistent application of this Regulation throughout the Union, the supervisory authorities shall cooperate with each other and, where relevant, with the Commission, through the consistency mechanism as set out in this Section.

heading: Dispute resolution by the Board
clause: The decision referred to in paragraph 1 shall be adopted within one month from the referral of the subject-matter by a two-thirds majority of the members of the Board.

heading: Dispute resolution by the Board
clause: The decision referred to in paragraph 1 shall be reasoned and addressed to the lead supervisory authority and all the supervisory authorities concerned and binding on them.

heading: Dispute resolution by the Board
clause: Where the Board has been unable to adopt a decision within the periods referred to in paragraph 2, it shall adopt its decision within two weeks following the expiration of the second month referred to in paragraph 2 by a simple majority of the members of the Board.

heading: Dispute resolution by the Board
clause: Where the members of the Board are split, the decision shall by adopted by the vote of its Chair.

heading: Dispute resolution by the Board
clause: The supervisory authorities concerned shall not adopt a decision on the subject matter submitted to the Board under paragraph 1 during the periods referred to in paragraphs 2 and 3.

clause: The decision shall be published on the website of the Board without delay after the supervisory authority has notified the final decision referred to in paragraph 6.

heading: Dispute resolution by the Board
clause: The lead supervisory authority or, as the case may be, the supervisory authority with which the complaint has been lodged shall adopt its final decision on the basis of the decision referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article, without undue delay and at the latest by one month after the Board has notified its decision.

heading: Dispute resolution by the Board
clause: The lead supervisory authority or, as the case may be, the supervisory authority with which the complaint has been lodged, shall inform the Board of the date when its final decision is notified respectively to the controller or the processor and to the data subject.

heading: Dispute resolution by the Board
clause: The final decision of the supervisory authorities concerned shall be adopted under the terms of Article 60(7), (8) and (9).

heading: Dispute resolution by the Board
clause: The final decision shall refer to the decision referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article and shall specify that the decision referred to in that paragraph will be published on the website of the Board in accordance with paragraph 5 of this Article.

heading: Dispute resolution by the Board
clause: The final decision shall attach the decision referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article.

heading: Urgency procedure
clause: In exceptional circumstances, where a supervisory authority concerned considers that there is an urgent need to act in order to protect the rights and freedoms of data subjects, it may, by way of derogation from the consistency mechanism referred to in Articles 63, 64 and 65 or the procedure referred to in Article 60, immediately adopt provisional measures intended to produce legal effects on its own territory with a specified period of validity which shall not exceed three months.

heading: Urgency procedure
clause: The supervisory authority shall, without delay, communicate those measures and the reasons for adopting them to the other supervisory authorities concerned, to the Board and to the Commission.

heading: Urgency procedure

clause: The European Data Protection Board (the ‘Board’) is hereby established as a body of the Union and shall have legal personality.

clause: Without prejudice to requests by the Commission referred to in point (b) of Article 70(1) and in Article 70(2), the Board shall, in the performance of its tasks or the exercise of its powers, neither seek nor take instructions from anybody.

heading: Right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority
clause: The supervisory authority with which the complaint has been lodged shall inform the complainant on the progress and the outcome of the complaint including the possibility of a judicial remedy pursuant to Article 78.

heading: Right to an effective judicial remedy against a supervisory authority
clause: Proceedings against a supervisory authority shall be brought before the courts of the Member State where the supervisory authority is established.

heading: Right to an effective judicial remedy against a supervisory authority
clause: Where proceedings are brought against a decision of a supervisory authority which was preceded by an opinion or a decision of the Board in the consistency mechanism, the supervisory authority shall forward that opinion or decision to the court.

heading: Right to an effective judicial remedy against a controller or processor
clause: Proceedings against a controller or a processor shall be brought before the courts of the Member State where the controller or processor has an establishment.

heading: Suspension of proceedings
clause: Where a competent court of a Member State has information on proceedings, concerning the same subject matter as regards processing by the same controller or processor, that are pending in a court in another Member State, it shall contact that court in the other Member State to confirm the existence of such proceedings.

heading: Right to compensation and liability
clause: A controller or processor shall be exempt from liability under paragraph 2 if it proves that it is not in any way responsible for the event giving rise to the damage.

heading: Right to compensation and liability
clause: Where more than one controller or processor, or both a controller and a processor, are involved in the same processing and where they are, under paragraphs 2 and 3, responsible for any damage caused by processing, each controller or processor shall be held liable for the entire damage in order to ensure effective compensation of the data subject.

heading: Right to compensation and liability
clause: Court proceedings for exercising the right to receive compensation shall be brought before the courts competent under the law of the Member State referred to in Article 79(2).

heading: General conditions for imposing administrative fines
clause: Each supervisory authority shall ensure that the imposition of administrative fines pursuant to this Article in respect of infringements of this Regulation referred to in paragraphs 4, 5 and 6 shall in each individual case be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.

heading: General conditions for imposing administrative fines
clause: Each supervisory authority shall ensure that the imposition of administrative fines pursuant to this Article in respect of infringements of this Regulation referred to in paragraphs 4, 5 and 6 shall in each individual case be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.

heading: General conditions for imposing administrative fines
clause: Administrative fines shall, depending on the circumstances of each individual case, be imposed in addition to, or instead of, measures referred to in points (a) to (h) and (j) of Article 58(2).

heading: General conditions for imposing administrative fines

heading: General conditions for imposing administrative fines
clause: If a controller or processor intentionally or negligently, for the same or linked processing operations, infringes several provisions of this Regulation, the total amount of the administrative fine shall not exceed the amount specified for the gravest infringement.

heading: General conditions for imposing administrative fines

heading: General conditions for imposing administrative fines
clause: Infringements of the following provisions shall, in accordance with paragraph 2, be subject to administrative fines up to 20 000 000 EUR, or in the case of an undertaking, up to 4 % of the total worldwide annual turnover of the preceding financial year, whichever is higher:

heading: General conditions for imposing administrative fines
clause: Non-compliance with an order by the supervisory authority as referred to in Article 58(2) shall, in accordance with paragraph 2 of this Article, be subject to administrative fines up to 20 000 000 EUR, or in the case of an undertaking, up to 4 % of the total worldwide annual turnover of the preceding financial year, whichever is higher.

heading: General conditions for imposing administrative fines
clause: The exercise by the supervisory authority of its powers under this Article shall be subject to appropriate procedural safeguards in accordance with Union and Member State law, including effective judicial remedy and due process.

heading: General conditions for imposing administrative fines
clause: In any event, the fines imposed shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.

heading: Penalties
clause: Member States shall lay down the rules on other penalties applicable to infringements of this Regulation in particular for infringements which are not subject to administrative fines pursuant to Article 83, and shall take all measures necessary to ensure that they are implemented.

heading: Processing and freedom of expression and information
